title: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages
body: datasette #3046: Don't serve link: rel=next HTTP headers to Firefox for HTML pages I was looking at the Firefox network panel today when I noticed that requests to a Datasette table page were triggering an HTTP prefetch to the next page of rows in that table. This was happening because Datasette pages serve an HTTP link header like this: link: <https://latest.datasette.io/fixtures/compound_three_primary_keys?_next=a%2Cd%2Cv>; rel="next" This is bad. A tiny fraction of the visitors to one of those pages will click the "next" link, which means their browser is fetching unnecessary data and the Datasette server is having to render an entire page that then gets thrown away. I dug in and learned that Firefox has an issue that has been open for 24 years about this behavior... And one of the early comments on that issue links to my blog post from 2002 complaining about this feature. I hadn't just forgotten that I had written about it, I had forgotten the feature entirely! body:
Entire MacOS running in your terminal.

README 節錄：# terminal-mac A separate macOS desktop for computer-use agents, viewed and controlled from a terminal. `terminal-mac` is an early release candidate for Apple silicon. Apple Virtualization runs a real macOS guest. A bundled helper **inside that guest** captures its screen and posts input events. A terminal viewer streams that screen using Kitty or iTerm2 graphics. Agent commands use the same helper without moving the physical Mac's pointer or changing its clipboard. The guest is a separate Mac: it has its own apps, files, accounts and permissions. It does not inherit your running host apps or signed-in sessions. The VM still consumes host CPU, memory and storage. ## Requirements - Apple silicon Mac, macOS 14 or later. - No development tools are needed for a prebuilt release. Maintainers need Xcode 16 or later / Swift 6 to build. - Internet on first run to download macOS directly from Apple, or an existing compatible `.ipsw`. - Space for the cached restore image and a growing VM disk (64 GiB logical size by default). - Ghostty, Kitty or iTerm2 for the inline viewer. Other terminals can use the native VM window and agent CLI. tmux passthrough and automatic terminal splits are not implemented. ## Install and run ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/govijr/terminal-mac/releases/latest/download/get.sh | bash ``` The installer downloads the latest release and verifies its SHA-256 before installing. To learn more about this I built a honeypot that resembled perfectly the Danfoss AK-SM 800A and Dixell XWEB interfaces. Both of them are recognized on Shodan as real ones (an not as honeypots). It’s one Python file using only the standard library, and it builds on eppser/danfoss-ak-sm-decoy and public research by Synacktiv, Claroty and Ironhackers. Things that were fun to get right: - Matching real units. I used Shodan records of real devices to match header order, page titles, certificate fields and TLS versions. The Danfoss persona sends nginx headers in the same order as a real AK-SM 800A. The Dixell persona sends no Server header and pads its page to exactly 8,202 bytes. - Recognising exploit attempts. It recognises CVE-2025-41450, the Danfoss “code of the day” login bypass, and records whether the submitted code is correct for today. It also tags attempts targeting three other Danfoss CVEs and the XWEB vulnerabilities. - Letting them in. Default logins open a fake store dashboard with defrost buttons, so you see the second move, not just the first. Nothing behind it is real. Two instances have been live for a day. So far they’ve only seen generic scanners and Shodan’s crawler, which is called refrigerator.census.shodan.io. Feedback welcome, es

title: Leviidev/Henge
body:
Emulate macOS on iOS and iPadOS

README 節錄： Henge macOS on your iPhone and iPad. Install · How it works · Website · Releases Download macOS, install it on the device, and use it. - **Own emulator** — iOS gives apps no hypervisor, so Henge runs the Mac's arm64 code through its own JIT, with its own MMU and devices. It doesn't use QEMU or Virtualization.framework. - **Installs on the device** — Henge downloads Apple's restore image and restores it the way a Mac does. No Mac needed, and nothing is decrypted or patched. - **Graphics** — macOS draws through a virtual GPU, and Henge replays its commands with Metal. Safari and Electron apps like Discord draw on it. - **Touch** — The screen is a trackpad: hold to drag, two fingers to scroll. Esc, Tab, Control, Option and Command sit above the keyboard. - **Keyboard and mouse** — On iPad, a Magic Keyboard or a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse drive the Mac directly. - **External display** — During a Mac session, connect a display with a video-capable USB-C cable or a USB-C/HDMI dock. The mode activates automatically: the monitor shows the Mac, while the iPhone or iPad keeps its trackpad and keyboard controls. Disconnect to return the image to the device. The existing guest resolution is preserved. On iOS 17–26 the same happens through an older iOS route, not yet tried on hardware; outside a Mac session the display mirrors the device. Value your Steam stash in the terminal and print it as a share card: per game, per market, what sold and what sits. One Windows portable build, no account.

Every number carries its venue and window. `LOWEST` is the floor listing right now. `AVG` is the mean of real sales over a window you pick. Steam money is wallet funds; everything else is cash, and the two are never mixed silently.
